List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on

(Ministries: Commerce and Industry; Health and Family Welfare; Heavy

Total number of questions—20
WIN2/NSESSION\3848RS 56
Declaring carpenters as SC
†*181. SHRI KRIPAL PARMAR: Will
the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE AND
EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether some MPs from Himachal
Pradesh as well as some members of the
State Assembly repeatedly requested for
declaration of carpenters as SC as in case
of black-smiths of that State;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) what is the present status in this
regard?
Free treatment for AIDS
*182. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the
Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that India has the
second largest number of patients of HIV/
AIDS;
(b) whether it is also a fact that there is
growing demand from the public that
Government should provide free treatment
for this disease, as it is not within the reach
of a patient of average means; and
(c) whether any proposal is under
Government’s consideration to offer free or
subsidized treatment to the patients, if so,
the details thereof?
Anti-India propaganda by BBC
*183. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: Will
the Minister of INFORMATION AND
BROADCASTING be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government’s attention has
been drawn to the TV programme,
"Question Time India", telecast over BBC
on Friday August 22, 2003 night relating
to Kashmir;
(b) if so, the reaction of Government
thereto; and
(c) what is Government’s control and
regulation on media agencies to prevent anti-
Indian propaganda and to ensure that they
confirm to publicity norms and principles
keeping in mind the policies of integration
and the Constitution of India?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

57
WIN2/NSESSION\3848RS 57
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Incentives for units in SEZ
*184. SHRIMATI BIMBA RAIKAR:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
extend additional incentives for setting up
of units in the Special Economic Zones
through a five year exemption from
Provident Fund/Employees State Insurance
liabilities for the entrepreneurs;
(b) whether it is also proposed to relax
labour laws and trade union Acts to attain
higher and committed productivity; and
(c) whether Government expect that
these incentives would spur growth of the
existing SEZs and also the new ones coming
up especially in Padubidri in Dakshina
Kannada region?
Misappropriation of tribal funds
†*185. SHRI ABHAY KANT
PRASAD: Will the Minister of TRIBAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government’s attention has
been drawn towards the issue of
misappropriation of Central funds provided
for development of tribals by the officers of
Bihar and Jharkhand Governments;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the details of action being taken by
Government; and
(d) the steps taken to prevent such
misappropriation of funds in future?
Growth of core sector industries
*186. DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
SHRI VAYALAR RAVI:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether growth of six core sector
industries sharply declined to 2.6 per cent in
July 2003 as compared to 10.2 per cent in
July, 2002;
(b) if so, whether between April and
July 2003, the infrastructure sector grew
by 3.6 per cent as compared to 7.2 per cent
in 2002;
(c) whether this was core sector's worst
performance since September 2002, when
it grew by1.7 per cent;
(d) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(e) to what extent this core sector has
been able to increase its growth during
2003-04?
Prices of cement
*187. SHRI V.V. RAGHAVAN:
SHRI GAYA SINGH:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there has
been a sudden spurt in prices of cement
recently due to the play of cartels in the
industry; and
(b) if so, the details thereof and
Government's reaction thereto?
Objectionable advertisements
on TV
*188. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY
SIRIGIREDDY: Will the Minister of
INFORMATION AND
BROADCASTING be pleased to state:
(a) the steps his Ministry and the
Advertising Standards Council of India
(ASCI) are taking under the Cable TV
Regulation Act and the code prescribed by
the ASCI in order to check the menace of
objectionable advertisements on TV
Channels;

Minister of URBAN DEVELOPMENT

(a) the number of DDA's residential
schemes for flats and plots;
(b) the number of people on waiting list,
scheme-wise and category-wise;
(c) the criteria for allotment to the
waitliste

New grain export policy
1233. SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN:
SHRI EKANATH K.
THAKUR:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether the new grain export policy
requires the exporter to buy grains directly
from market;
(b) if so, the details thereof including the
device of transportation and storage of the
grains before export;
(c) whether any studies have been
conducted on the impact of this policy on
the storage and distribution of grains for
domestic purpose and Public Distribution
System;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, whether detailed studies
would be conducted before implementing
the new grain export policy?
Export and Import
†1234. SHRI KAPIL SIBAL:
SHRI LAJPAT RAI:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that export from
the country and import in to the country
have continuously increased during the last
years;
(b) if so, the import and export in terms
of value during the years 2000-01,
2001-02 and 2002-03; and
(c) the value of import and export of
petroleum products during the above period?
Import of life saving medicines
1235. SHRI K. KALAVENKATA
RAO:
SHRI ABANI ROY:
SHRI C. RAMACHAND-
RAIAH:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have struck a

270
WIN2/NSESSION\3849RSW 270
deal with WTO allowing India to import
life saving medicines to fight AIDS,
tuberculosis and other epidemics;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether the duty structure on these
life saving drugs has been decided; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Export growth
1236. SHRI V.V. RAGHAVAN:
SHRI GAYA SINGH:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the export
growth during the first half of the current
financial year has not been satisfactory as
it came down to 10 per cent from 20 per
cent during the same period last year; and
(b) if so, the details thereof and
Government's reaction thereto?
Export of tea to Pakistan
1237. SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI  REDDY:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether a Pakistani tea delegation
visited India in September, 2003 and had
discussions with Government;
(b) whether Government have agreed
to consider an incentive linked package for
tea exports to Pakistan;
(c) whether all the concessions as
recommended by the Pakistan Government
have been fully met;
(d) if so, whether India has exported 10
million kg. of tea to Pakistan during the
current fiscal year;
(e) if so, the other steps being taken to
export more tea to Pakistan; and
(f) to what extent it has been welcomed
by the Pakistan Government?
Trade relations with China
1238. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether trade agreement with China
signed during the Prime Minister's visit have
improved the trade relations with China;
(b) if so, whether India and China have
decided to establish joint study group on
economic cooperation;
(c) whether the Confedration of Indian
Industry has entered into a fresh
Memorandum of Understanding with the
All-China Federation of Industry and
Commerce in October, 2003;
(d) if so, whether his Ministry has
sought Cabinet approval for offer list
forwarded by China and exchange of tariff
concessions with that country under
Bangkok Agreement; and
(e) if so, to what extent Government
have approved and conveyed to Chinese
Government?
Export of wheat to Iraq
1239. DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
DR. A. R. KIDWAI:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Indian business delegation
that went to Iraq was successful in reviving
contracts worth Rs. 300 crores for export
of three lakh tonnes of wheat to Iraq under
the United Nation's oil-for-food
programme;

271
WIN2/NSESSION\3849RSW 271
(b) if so, whether Government in Iraq
has approved to revive export of wheat
contracts for which agreements were
already signed but shipments could not go
through due to war;
(c) whether before war, there was an
agreement of supplying wheat to Iraq;
(d) if so, the quantity of wheat Iraq has
agreed to import from India; and
(e) the arrangements made to supply
the same?
Trade between India and UK

MEENA:
